ego.name: Zaha Hadid
ego.summary: Zaha Hadid was an Iraqi British architect, artist, and designer whose paintings and buildings used fractured and fluid geometry. After early recognition for unbuilt designs, she completed projects internationally and became the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

connections.relationship_description: Hadid's father was an Iraqi industrialist, political figure, and former finance minister who raised her in an upper-class Baghdad household.
connections.notes: He was also known as Mohammed Hadid.

connections.relationship_description: Hadid's mother was an artist from Mosul. She and Muhammad al-Hajj Husayn Hadid raised Hadid in Baghdad.
connections.notes: She is also spelled Wajiha Sabonji.

connections.relationship_description: Hadid's brother was a writer, accountant, and expert on Arab affairs.
Koolhaas taught Hadid at the Architectural Association School of Architecture and then employed her at the Office for Metropolitan Architecture after her 1977 graduation.
connections.notes: Koolhaas described Hadid at graduation as "a planet in her own orbit."

connections.relationship_description: Zenghelis was one of Hadid's teachers at the Architectural Association and later worked with her at the Office for Metropolitan Architecture in Rotterdam.
connections.notes: He called her the most outstanding pupil he had taught.

connections.relationship_description: Schumacher began his association with Hadid's practice after encountering The Peak design. He later became a partner and worked with her on major projects.
connections.notes: Hadid described Schumacher as an enormous support and an incredible enrichment to her work.

connections.relationship_description: As Vitra's president-director general, Fehlbaum commissioned Hadid to design the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein, completed in 1993.
connections.notes: As Vitra's president-director general, Fehlbaum commissioned the Vitra Fire Station in Weil am Rhein.

connections.relationship_description: Hadid was one of three children of Muhammad Hadid and Wajiha al-Sabunji, alongside her brothers Haytham and Foulath.
connections.notes: The supplied material provides little detail about his relationship with Hadid beyond their shared family.

connections.relationship_description: Tschumi taught Hadid during her architectural education at the Architectural Association School of Architecture after she moved to London in 1972.
The structural engineer supported and encouraged Hadid during the early phase of her architectural career after she joined the Office for Metropolitan Architecture.
connections.notes: Rice supported and encouraged Hadid during the early stage of her career.

connections.relationship_description: The real estate developer commissioned Hadid to design Capital Hill Residence, his private home in Barvikha near Moscow, completed in 2018 after her death.
connections.notes: The project was designed during Hadid's lifetime and completed posthumously.

connections.relationship_description: Johnson co-curated the 1988 Museum of Modern Art exhibition Deconstructivism in Architecture, which presented Hadid among seven architects and expanded her international profile.
Wigley co-curated the 1988 Museum of Modern Art exhibition Deconstructivism in Architecture, which included Hadid among seven architects.
Hadid and the British architectural artist developed an unexecuted proposal for Vienna's Spittelau Viaducts Housing Project that integrated Clarke's glass mosaic and stained-glass artwork.
connections.notes: Clarke developed a new mouth-blown glass type for the project, which he called Zaha-Glas.

connections.relationship_description: Obrist interviewed Hadid for his long-running interview archive and included their conversation in his Conversation Series.
connections.notes: Their documented interview preserved Hadid's architectural ideas within contemporary art and design discourse.

connections.relationship_description: As head of the Pritzker Prize jury, Pritzker announced Hadid's 2004 award.
connections.notes: Hadid was the first woman to receive the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

category_summaries.summary: Hadid grew up in Baghdad in a family whose members worked in business, public life, art, and writing. Her father, Muhammad al-Hajj Husayn Hadid, was an industrialist and political figure. Her mother, Wajiha al-Sabunji, was an artist from Mosul. Her brothers Foulath and Haytham remained part of her family history.

Hadid studied at London's Architectural Association School of Architecture after mathematics studies in Beirut. Rem Koolhaas, Elia Zenghelis, and Bernard Tschumi taught her there. After graduating in 1977, she worked with Koolhaas and Zenghelis at the Office for Metropolitan Architecture in Rotterdam.

Hadid's professional circle links early encouragement, long-term collaboration, commissions, and public recognition. Peter Rice supported her early career. Patrik Schumacher became a long-term colleague and partner. Rolf Fehlbaum commissioned the Vitra Fire Station, and Thomas Pritzker announced her 2004 Pritzker Architecture Prize.

Curators and collaborators connected Hadid's work with experimental architecture and art. Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley included her in the 1988 Museum of Modern Art exhibition Deconstructivism in Architecture. Brian Clarke collaborated with her on an unbuilt Vienna housing proposal, and Hans Ulrich Obrist recorded an interview with her.
